title: Epiblast is not ectoderm

objective.text: Distinguish the epiblast from the ectoderm it leaves behind.

body.general: Is the epiblast just another name for ectoderm? No [f1,f3]. The epiblast is the top layer of the two-layered disc in week 2 [f1]. In week 3 many of its cells move in through the streak and become endoderm and mesoderm [f2]. Only the cells left behind are ectoderm [f3]. So the epiblast is the parent of all three germ layers, and ectoderm is just one of them [f4].
body.mbbs: The epiblast is the dorsal layer of the bilaminar disc in week 2 [f1]. In week 3 its cells ingress through the primitive streak to form endoderm and mesoderm [f2]. Only the cells that stay behind become ectoderm [f3]. So all three germ layers derive from the epiblast, and together they build every tissue of the embryo [f4]. 'Epiblast' names the week-2 layer; 'ectoderm' names what remains of it after gastrulation [f1,f3].

facts.text: The epiblast is the upper layer of the two-layered disc in week 2.
In week 3, epiblast cells moving in through the streak form endoderm and mesoderm.
The cells that stay in the epiblast become ectoderm.
So all three germ layers come from the epiblast, and together they build every tissue of the embryo.
Beyond Langman: human single-cell and spatial studies at stage 7 find epiblast, streak, new mesoderm, endoderm and primordial germ cells side by side.

misconceptions.wrong: Epiblast and ectoderm are the same thing.
misconceptions.right: The epiblast is the week-2 upper layer; ectoderm is only the part left after cells move in.

misconceptions.wrong: The three germ layers come from different starting layers.
misconceptions.right: All three come from the epiblast.

options: Ectoderm is the part of the epiblast left after cells move in
Ectoderm and epiblast are two names for one layer
checks.why: The epiblast gives rise to all three layers; ectoderm is what stays behind.

checks.prompt: All three germ layers come from which layer?
checks.why: Endoderm and mesoderm move in from the epiblast, and ectoderm is the epiblast left behind.

adult: Every tissue of the body traces back to the epiblast [f4].

remember.a: The upper layer of the two-layered disc in week 2 [f1].

remember.q: Which part of the epiblast becomes ectoderm?
remember.a: The cells that stay behind instead of moving in [f3].
